subject.title: Feature request: first-class .env / environment-backed secret config UX

question: What SecretRef source metadata may Control UI and CLI expose for env-backed secrets, and should this issue remain the canonical tracker for the Control UI UX portion?
rationale: The code already supports env-backed SecretRefs; the remaining choice is how much source, variable-name, and resolution metadata is safe and desirable to reveal across UI and CLI surfaces.

options.title: Approve Conservative Source-Aware UX
options.body: Show masked `config`/`env`/`unset` state and resolved/unresolved status, with env variable names shown only where maintainers accept that disclosure.

options.title: Consolidate Before Implementation
options.body: Move the remaining Control UI requirements into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/16351 and keep one broader config-secret UX tracker.

options.title: Defer UI Disclosure
options.body: Keep current read-only structured SecretRef rendering and improve docs/CLI guidance until a security review defines the metadata policy.

recommendation.title: Approve Conservative Source-Aware UX
recommendation.body: Show masked `config`/`env`/`unset` state and resolved/unresolved status, with env variable names shown only where maintainers accept that disclosure.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits on top of the SecretRef runtime/redaction contract that Josh most directly shaped through merged history.
